messages.text: Fritz misses out on ATP Finals after squandering chance to beat Alcaraz

metadata.summary: Taylor Fritz missed out on claiming the last spot at the ATP Finals in Turin later this month after squandering two match points in his Paris Masters quarter-final defeat to Carlos Alcaraz.
metadata.content: Paris Masters: Taylor Fritz squanders match points against Carlos Alcaraz as defeat ends hopes of reaching ATP Finals | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Paris Masters: Taylor Fritz squanders match points against Carlos Alcaraz as defeat ends hopes of reaching ATP Finals Season-ending ATP Finals live on Sky Sports from November 15-22 , with Spanish youngster Rafael Jodar taking eighth and final spot after Taylor Fritz's defeat to already-qualified Carlos Alcaraz in Paris; Frances Tiafoe's place secured earlier on Friday Friday 6 November 2026 22:48, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from a thrilling quarter-final at the Paris Masters as Carlos Alcaraz fought from a set down to beat Taylor Fritz Taylor Fritz missed out on claiming the last spot at the ATP Finals in Turin later this month after squandering two match points in his Paris Masters quarter-final defeat to Carlos Alcaraz. Fritz would have reached the end-of-season event in Italy at Rafael Jodar's expense had he beaten Alcaraz to make the last four. He looked poised to do that after twice finding himself a point from victory in the second set, once on his opponent's serve at 5-3 up and then on his own with the score at 5-4. However, Alcaraz rallied during a high-quality match to triumph 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 and ensure he will be joined by compatriot Jodar at the ATP Finals from November 15-22, live on Sky Sports . metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc says he will make "significant" setup changes to his car after "one of the worst feelings" in practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Charles Leclerc plans 'significant' Ferrari car changes as Lewis Hamilton rues 'difficult' Brazil practice | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Charles Leclerc plans 'significant' Ferrari car changes as Lewis Hamilton rues 'difficult' Brazil practice Ferrari were off the pace compared to Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull on Friday in Brazil with both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton unhappy about the car's balance; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 6 November 2026 22:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix Charles Leclerc says he will make "significant" setup changes to his car after "one of the worst feelings" in practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Leclerc was seven tenths off pace-setter Kimi Antonelli in second practice and Lewis Hamilton was nearly half a second behind as Ferrari trailed Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull on Friday. It was a contrast to their recent pace with Ferrari claiming a podium position in the last four races but Leclerc is hoping they can turn that around in final practice on Saturday at 2.30pm and qualifying at 6pm, live on Sky Sports F1 . messages.text: New champion Antonelli tops Brazil practice

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli completed an impressive first day back on track as F1's new world champion to set the pace in second practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest for Mercedes in second practice at Interlagos ahead of Lando Norris in upgraded McLaren | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest for Mercedes in second practice at Interlagos ahead of Lando Norris in upgraded McLaren F1's new world champion sets the pace from its outgoing one on the first day in Brazil; Max Verstappen third fastest but Ferraris off pace on short runs; Rain forecast over weekend; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Friday 6 November 2026 21:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Kimi Antonelli completed an impressive first day back on track as F1's new world champion to set the pace in second practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Five days after becoming the sport's youngest title winner in Mexico, Antonelli followed up his second-fastest time from first practice with the quickest of the more representative second session around the undulating Interlagos lap. Antonelli was the only driver to lap below 71 seconds with his benchmark time of 1:10.763 proving two tenths of a second quicker than nearest challengers Lando Norris, the P1 pacesetter , and Max Verstappen. messages.text: Patriots' Henderson sidelined by 'unexplained neurological symptoms'

metadata.summary: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson says a series of "unexplained neurological symptoms" are the reason for his recent absence.
metadata.content: NFL: New England Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson has been absent due to 'unexplained neurological symptoms' | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: New England Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson has been absent due to 'unexplained neurological symptoms' TreVeyon Henderson reveals on social media that he has spent several days in hospital; cause of symptoms still unknown but 24-year-old says results have been "reassuring"; Henderson missed the New England Patriots' win over the Miami Dolphins last weekend Friday 6 November 2026 19:46, UK Image: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has been absent due to 'unexplained neurological symptoms' New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson says a series of "unexplained neurological symptoms" are the reason for his recent absence. Henderson has not practised since late October, when he was listed as having an illness, and missed Sunday's 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. The player revealed in a social media post on Friday that he has spent a number of days in hospital after issues with his strength and coordination. The cause of the problem remains "unknown and unexplainable", although Henderson says results have been "reassuring". messages.text: ‘The message was clear’ - Vasseur holds Hamilton-Leclerc meeting after clash

metadata.summary: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says he reminded Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc that the team comes first after their first-lap clash in Mexico in a meeting ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur confirms Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc meeting after Mexico clash ahead of Sao Paulo GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur confirms Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc meeting after Mexico clash ahead of Sao Paulo GP Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Frederic Vasseur spoke on Thursday evening at Interlagos four days on from team-mates' first-lap incident in Mexico; Vasseur says "the message was clear and will stay clear"; watch Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Friday 6 November 2026 19:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says he reminded Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc that the team comes first after their first-lap clash in Mexico in a meeting ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. The lap-one incident between the Ferrari drivers in last Sunday's race, which saw both cars run wide track at Turn Four in battle for the lead, ultimately opened the door for Red Bull's Max Verstappen to win the race. Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future.
